steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Horror is a genre designed to elicit fear, dread and disgust, confronting audiences with the transgressive, the unknown and the repressed.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Core horror conventions include isolation, the monstrous Other, transgression of boundaries, the return of the repressed and the struggle for survival.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Horror sub-genres include slasher, supernatural, psychological, body horror, found footage, folk horror and gothic horror.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Carol Clover's 'final girl' theory identifies the last surviving female character in slasher films as the figure with whom the audience ultimately identifies.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always connect horror conventions to their emotional or psychological effect on the audience. Name specific theorists when relevant — Clover for the final girl, Kristeva for the abject, Freud for the uncanny. Identify which sub-genre your film belongs to and how it uses or challenges that sub-genre's conventions. Discuss the monster as metaphor — what real-world anxiety does it embody? Consider the film's cultural context: when was it made, and what fears were current in society at that time?
